classification.difficultyReason: Construct a cooling model, determine its constant from an observation and solve for a specified temperature.

content.prompt:
A pot of coffee is heated to $95^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

The room temperature is a constant $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and the coffee cools down to $55^\circ\mathrm{C}$ after 5 minutes.

The cooling rate is proportional to the difference between the coffee and room temperatures.

When will the coffee reach optimal drinking temperature, $60^\circ\mathrm{C}$? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $T$ be the coffee temperature in degrees Celsius and $t$ the time in minutes after cooling begins.

$$\begin{align*}
\frac{dT}{dt}&=k(T-25),\qquad k<0\\
T&=25+Ae^{kt}\\
95&=25+A\\
A&=70
\end{align*}$$

Using $T(5)=55$:

$$\begin{align*}
55&=25+70e^{5k}\\
30&=70e^{5k}\\
e^{5k}&=\frac37\\
5k&=\ln\left(\frac37\right)\\
k&=\frac{\ln(3/7)}5
\end{align*}$$

Thus $T=25+70e^{[\ln(3/7)/5]t}$. For $T=60$:

$$\begin{align*}
60&=25+70e^{kt}\\
35&=70e^{kt}\\
e^{kt}&=\frac12\\
kt&=\ln\left(\frac12\right)\\
t&=\frac{\ln(1/2)}k\\
t&=\frac{5\ln(1/2)}{\ln(3/7)}\\
t&\approx4.09\text{ minutes}.
\end{align*}$$
